 Judgment
Dated this the 8th day of April , 2025 The 3rd respondent in O.P.(M.V.) No. 660/ 2012 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Tirur, is the appellant.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.

The O.P. was filed under under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, by the parents, wife,
minor child and siblings of the deceased Sajeev, who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 13.03.2012.

According to them, on 13.03.2012, at about 3 p.m., while the deceased was riding a motorcycle, a car bearing Reg.No.KL-12-E-5685 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner, knocked him down and as a result of which he sustained serious injuries and later on he succumbed to the injuries, on 20.03.2012, while under treatment.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P.
was Rs.23,00,000/- (Claim limited to 22,00,000/-).
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A12.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs. 17,25,000/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the 3rd respondent preferred this appeal.

Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri. Jaocb P. Mathew, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the appellant/3rd respondent and Sri. A. Krishnan the learned Counsel appearing for the claimants.
10.
The Point:

One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is that, at the time of the accident, the deceased had no valid driving licence and there was contributory negligence on his part.
However, 2025:KER:32984 in this case, the Police filed Ext.A4 charge sheet against the 2nd respondent alone and no contributory negligence was found against the deceased.
No contra evidence was adduced by the respondents.

Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, it is to be held that the accident occurred only due to the negligence of the 2nd respondent and that there was no contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
Similarly, for the reason that there was no valid driving licence for the deceased at the time of the accident, no presumption can be drawn to the effect that, he had contributed to the accident.

The learned Standing Counsel would argue that, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs. 2,00,000/-
towards love and affection in addition to Rs.25,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.75,000/-
towards loss of consortium, which, according to him are on the higher side.

On the other hand, the learned counsel for the petitioners would argue that, the notional income of the deceased as fixed by the Tribunal is on the lower side and also argue that the compensation awarded on the other heads are also on lower side.
As per the claim petition, the deceased was working as workshop mechanic, getting a monthly income of Rs. 6,000/- per month.

The Tribunal 2025:KER:32984 also fixed his monthly income at Rs. 6,000/-
11.

As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, during the year 2012 will come to Rs.8,500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the learned counsel prayed for fixing the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.8,500/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

Since the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2012 will come to Rs.8,500/-, in order to award just and reasonable compensation, in the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra), the notional income of the petitioner is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at RS.8,500/-.
12.
On the date of accident, the deceased was aged 29 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is liable to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 17, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of dependency will come to Rs.18,20,700/-.
13. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs. 25,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.75,000/- towards loss of consortium and Rs.2,00,000/- towards love and affection.
The Tribunal has not awarded any amount on the heads loss of estate.

In the light of the decision in Pranay Sethi (supra), the appellants are entitled to get a consolidated sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.15,000/-
towards funeral expenses, and the dependents (parents, children and spouse) are entitled to get a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium, with an increase of 10% in every three years.

Therefore, towards loss of estate and funeral expense they are entitled to get a sum of Rs.18,150/-
each.

Towards loss of consortium, petitioners together are entitled to get a sum of Rs.1,93,600/-
(48,400 x4).
14.

Since compensation for loss of consortium was given, further compensation for love and affection cannot be granted, in view of the decision in New India Assurance Company Ltd. v.
Somwati and Others, (2020)9 SCC 644.

sentences.text: Therefore, the compensation awarded towards love and affection is to be deducted.
15. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has 2025:KER:32984 awarded Rs.20,000/-, which according to the learned counsel for the petitioners, is on the lower side.
The deceased died in this case 7 or 8 days after the accident.

In the above circumstances, I hold that the compensation awarded towards pain and suffering is on the lower side, and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.35,000/-
16.
Though Rs.173,000/- is awarded on the head 'Medical, Bystander, funeral and post funeral expenses', it appears that there is medical bills alone for Rs.172217/-.
Therefore, the said amount is limited to medical expenses.
17. The learned Standing Counsel also challenge the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal at 9%.
Considering the facts, I hold that interest at the 8% will be a reasonable rate, for entire amount.
18. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
19. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants

are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.22,66,600/-
